turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Hi Elena, thanks for making the time. I know pricing was the big open item from last week, so I want to walk you through the plans and leave plenty of room for questions.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: Perfect. My VP is going to ask me two things: what does it cost per seat, and what happens when we scale past fifty users.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Great questions. So we have three tiers. Team is nineteen dollars per seat per month, Growth is thirty-four, and Enterprise is custom. Growth is where most teams your size land.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: Thirty-four is honestly higher than what we're paying for our current tool. That's going to be the first objection internally.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: I hear you. The way I'd frame it is the current tool doesn't do the automated call summaries, and that's the piece your team said was eating an hour a day.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: That's fair. The time savings is real. If we go past fifty seats, does the per-seat price drop?

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Yes. At fifty seats we move you to volume pricing, which brings Growth down to twenty-eight a seat, and Enterprise unlocks SSO and the audit log.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: SSO is going to matter to our security team. They flagged it as a requirement for anything that touches customer calls.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Then Enterprise is probably the honest recommendation, even at your current headcount. I don't want to sell you Growth and have security block it in month two.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: I appreciate that. What's the Enterprise number look like for, say, forty seats?

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: For forty seats with SSO and the audit log, we'd be looking at roughly fifteen hundred a month, and I can hold that rate through the end of the quarter.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: Okay. That's a number I can actually take to my VP. Can you put all of this in a proposal I can forward?

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Absolutely. I'll send the proposal over by Friday with the forty-seat Enterprise pricing, the SSO details, and the security overview attached.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: That works. My VP is out Thursday, so Friday actually lines up well for our Monday review.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Then let's target Friday. One thing I'd flag: if security wants a full SOC 2 report, that goes through our compliance team and can take a few days, so it's worth kicking off early.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: Good call. I'll ask our security lead whether they need the full report or just the summary, and I'll let you know by Wednesday.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Perfect. So to recap: I send the proposal Friday, you confirm the SOC 2 scope Wednesday, and we regroup after your Monday review.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: That's the plan. Honestly, if the proposal lands the way this call did, I think we're in good shape to move forward this quarter.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Love to hear it. I'll get that proposal to you by Friday and we'll take it from there. Thanks Elena.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: Thanks Marcus, talk soon.
